title: measure/v1 output
description: The JSON payload agent-cost's `measure --format json` prints on stdout (exit 0). This is the cross-language conformance schema for D11 (multi-language stack support): agent-cost (Python, the producer and normative implementation) and any consumer written in another language (e.g. spec-lane's TypeScript AgentCostTelemetryAdapter) must agree on this exact shape. The schema was written by running agent-cost's actual `measure` command and reading agent_cost/cli.py's cmd_measure (payload construction), agent_cost/aggregate.py's Row.to_dict()/rows_totals(), and agent_cost/facts.py's SOURCE_QUALITY_VALUES directly -- it is a transcription of the real, current output, not a spec written from a description of intended behavior. The prose contract (what each field means, why measure exists, exit-code semantics) lives in agent-cost's own README ("Machine consumption: agent-cost measure" section) -- see docs/protocols/measure-v1.md for how that division of ownership works and why this schema does not duplicate that prose. DELIBERATELY UNLIKE every other contract in this repo (trace/v1, attribution/v1, estimate/v2, agent-metrics/v1), no object here sets `additionalProperties: false` -- see 'Open vs. closed schema' below. REQUIRED-FLOOR POLICY (sol review, compatibility floor -- not an immutable freeze): every key currently listed in a `required` array here is fixed for the lifetime of v1 -- it may never be REMOVED from `required` without a v2 (that would let a payload silently drop a field an existing consumer depends on), and a field that is optional today may never become required within v1 either (that would reject a still-valid OLDER producer's output that predates the new field -- the actual bug this floor policy exists to prevent). A brand-new field introduced by a future additive agent-cost change is added to `properties` as OPTIONAL (never to `required`) until/unless a `measure/v2` makes it part of the floor. See docs/protocols/measure-v1.md's Versioning section. Rules this schema alone cannot express, enforced instead as semantic checks in verify-fixtures.mjs: (1) every row's `tokens` MUST equal `priced_tokens + unpriced_tokens`. (2) a row's `pricing_status` MUST be "unpriced" if and only if its `unpriced_tokens > 0` (agent_cost/aggregate.py's build_rows ranks unpriced as the worst status and it wins outright the moment any one fact in the bucket is unpriced -- see that function's docstring). (3) a `totals` object (whether a session's or the top-level `total`'s) MUST equal the recomputed sum of its own `rows`. (4) the top-level `total.totals` MUST equal the sum, across every requested session, of that session's own `totals` (measure's `total` is the union of exactly the requested sessions, never a broader report). (5) `session_ids` and the keys of `sessions` MUST be the same set. (6) the top-level `data_quality.unpriced_tokens` MUST equal the sum of `total.rows[].unpriced_tokens`. (7) a session entry with `matched: false` MUST have an empty `rows` array and all-zero `totals` -- "no usage matched" and "usage matched but happened to net to zero" are different facts, and this schema alone cannot compare `matched` against its siblings. (8) the top-level `total.rows` MUST equal the (agent, model, token_kind)-dimensional re-aggregation of the union of every `sessions[*].rows` -- not just a scalar totals sum (check 4 above): two payloads can have identical `total.totals` scalars while `total.rows` attributes the same tokens to the wrong `agent`/`model`/`token_kind` bucket, which check 4 alone cannot catch. (9) the personal-dimension scan (contracts/shared/personal-dimensions.mjs) -- measure/v1 carries no per-actor identity at all, so any forbidden key anywhere in the payload is a contamination; this check does not depend on `additionalProperties` and still catches contamination in an open schema. Open vs. closed schema: agent-cost's own README states measure/v1's real versioning policy -- 'Within a major version, only additive changes (new fields) are made; a field being removed or changing meaning bumps the version.' A closed (`additionalProperties: false`) schema, the pattern this repo otherwise uses for its own playbook-owned/frozen protocols, would reject a legitimately current `measure/v1` payload the moment agent-cost adds a field under that policy -- a false-positive conformance failure against the real producer. This mirrors spec-lane's own `AgentCostRowSchema`/`AgentCostMeasureResultSchema` (packages/schemas/src/agent-cost.ts), which already use `.passthrough()`/unknown-key-tolerant parsing for exactly this reason. `required` is still enforced in full -- this schema only stops short of forbidding *extra* keys, it never stops checking for the documented minimum set (and, per the required-floor policy above, never grows that minimum set within v1 either).

generated_at.description: Python's `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` -- always a numeric UTC offset ("+00:00"), never a "Z" suffix (that is only how request-side --since/--until accept input; it is never what agent-cost itself emits on output).

window.description: The --since/--until bounds actually applied, echoed back as the exact instant agent-cost resolved them to (not the caller's raw input string). Both null when the corresponding flag was omitted -- an unbounded window is never represented as an arbitrary sentinel date.

timezone.description: The --timezone value as given (e.g. "UTC", "Asia/Tokyo"); only affects date-only --since/--until parsing, since measure never buckets rows by month.

agent.description: The resolved --agent filter, sorted (agent_cost/cli.py: `sorted(agents)`) -- both agents when --agent was omitted.

session_ids.description: The requested --session-id values, in the order given, de-duplicated (agent_cost/cli.py: `list(dict.fromkeys(...))`). Always at least one -- measure exits 2 before producing any output if none was given.

sessions.description: One entry per requested session_id, keyed by that session_id. A session with no matching usage at all still gets an entry here (matched: false, empty rows, all-zero totals) -- measure never omits a requested session_id from this map.

total.description: The union of every requested session's facts, re-aggregated by agent/model/token-kind (never by session, never by month) -- NOT a global report over all locally recorded usage.

unpriced_tokens.description: Sum of total.rows[].unpriced_tokens -- scoped to the requested sessions, same as every other field here, never a global figure.

source_quality.description: One count per agent_cost/facts.py SOURCE_QUALITY_VALUES entry, scoped to facts belonging to the requested sessions only (agent_cost/cli.py builds this from `combined_facts`, not from every locally recorded fact). SOURCE_QUALITY_VALUES MAY grow a new named value in a future additive change (same policy as the rest of this payload); `ok`/`first_event_delta` are the current, required minimum, not a closed ceiling.

row.description: agent_cost/aggregate.py's Row.to_dict(). measure always groups by (agent, model, token-kind) and never by month (agent_cost/cli.py: `group_by = ("agent", "model", "token-kind")`), so `month` is always null on every row measure emits -- unlike `report`, which does bucket by month and would populate it.

token_kind.description: OPEN, not a closed enum -- unlike `agent`/`pricing_status` below. Currently-known values (agent_cost/facts.py's TOKEN_KINDS): input_nocache, cache_read, cache_write_5m, cache_write_1h, cache_write_unknown, output. A new token_kind is exactly the kind of additive change agent-cost's own versioning policy allows within v1 without a version bump (same as a new top-level/nested field), so this schema only requires a non-empty string, never membership in the current set -- an enum here would make the schema itself the breaking change the moment agent-cost adds one. See docs/protocols/measure-v1.md's 'Known token_kind values are producer/contract/consumer, not one shared verdict' for why a *consumer* is still free to fail closed on an unrecognized value even though this schema and agent-cost itself both accept it.

totals.description: agent_cost/aggregate.py's rows_totals() -- a plain sum of a set of rows, currently exactly these 5 keys (open to an additive 6th under agent-cost's own versioning policy -- see this schema's top-level description).
